title: Crimp a filled turnover in a hinged pastry press
instruction: Finish folding the press and squeeze it to seal the filled turnover. Reopen the press and leave the sealed turnover resting in the lower well.
context: A continuous crimp keeps the filling inside a hand pie. Counterhold the lower die while pressing the opposite tab, then reopen the die to check the seal before transferring the pastry to a tray.
setup: A four-inch polypropylene pastry press sits on a 215 × 116 × 32 mm work board with two locating pads. Both recessed halves have serrated rims and finger tabs. A detent holds the upper die at a 46° opening. A 101 mm round raw wrapper and a level teaspoon of thick fruit filling are loaded in the press. The bench is 747.5 mm high. Both YAM grippers start open and clear.
scoring: 0 if the wrapper does not fold around the filling. 0.25 if folded but the curved seam gapes or comes apart during reopening. 0.65 for a continuous crimp before the press is fully opened and hands clear. 1.0 when the press is reopened within 24° of flat and the sealed pastry rests in the lower well with both grippers clear for 0.6 seconds. A gap larger than 3 mm or exposed filling prevents full credit.
reset_notes: Use a fresh round wrapper and a level teaspoon of thick filling. Clean the press, set the lower die between the locating pads, and stage the loaded upper die in the opening detent.
fidelity: The press hinge and gripper contacts use rigid-body physics. Two thin dough lobes represent the wrapper. A force law approximates the response of moist dough against the upper die and the resistance of the completed seam. The filling is a cohesive mound.
scores: Demo: 1.0 in 356 actions. Dream-1: 0.0 after 720 actions.
